April Fool’s prank sends Linda flying

By ohtadmin
on September 16, 2026

BY ERIC LEVINE 810-452-2689 elevine@mihomepaper.com
FacebookTwitterEmailMessengerCopy LinkMessageShare

Linda Rowe is strapped under instructor Paul Helser after jumping out of the plane at 14,000 feet. Photo by Midwest Freefall

What started as an April Fool’s Day prank ended 14,000 feet in the air.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:03
Instaread

That’s the point where Linda Rowe, 88, jumped out of a single-wing Cessna – with a little help from a professional skydiver.

Rowe is a resident of Stonegate Village Assisted Living in Sandusky, where the enrichment director, Amanda Childers, played an April Fool’s Day joke on a group of residents.

Childers said she told the group of women that an airplane would be landing in front of the Argyle Street facility to take them for a parachute jump.

Rowe was the only one that piped up, “Sign me up, I’m ready to go.”

Five months later, Childers made it happen.

On Sept. 10, the 88-year-old former Palms area resident climbed into the Cessna with skydiving instructor Paul Helser, and three videographers, at Midwest Freefall in Ray.

“It’s rare,” said Randy Allison, owner of Midwest, for someone Rowe’s age to make the jump.

But jump she did, tightly strapped to Helser.

 

Rowe admits to being a little anxious when she was strapped-in, sitting in front of Helser, with her legs dangling out the plane’s door moments before the instructor “kind of lifted me” for the jump.

“We were above the clouds, it was beautiful,” said Rowe.

“I don’t know how to to describe the feeling, just kind of amazing.”

Childers, who brought eight other residents, and some of Rowe’s friends, to watch the event, estimates the jump lasted five to 10 minutes.

Rowe said the parachute landing felt like a slight bump.

“I was out of breath, my legs were tired.”

Rowe said her legs were still wobbly the following day, when she talked to the Sanilac County News.

The skydive was one of many adventures Rowe has taken.

Rowe, who spent her early years growing up in Ohio before the family moved to Pennsylvania, recalls playing a snare drum in the 1954 Rose Parade in Pasadena California.

She was a member of her high school’s marching band from Pittsburgh that was selected to play in the famous parade.

After high school, Rowe went on to earn a bachelor’s degree in education and teach physical education and recreation at South Redford High School in Michigan, and later, after earning a master’s degree, at a community college in Ohio.

During her summer breaks from teaching, and when she wasn’t working at children’s camps, Rowe set off on adventures.

She attended three Summer Olympics Games – in Mexico in 1968, in Munich, Germany in 1972 when a terrorist attack killed Israeli athletes, and in Montreal, Canada in 1976.

She also went whitewater rafting through the Grand Canyon, took days-long horseback riding trips in the Superstition Mountains in Arizona, and participated in archaeological digs.

Rowe now enjoys a quiet life at Stonegate, where she has resided for the last year.

However, that doesn’t mean she’s not up for another adventure.

“If something comes about and I think I could do it, I probably would,” said Rowe.

“You’ve had an amazing life, Linda,” said Childers.
